Per-entry verified (RFC 0032 wide-entry verification): Rails schema_definitions.rb:605-607 uses `[:integer, :bigint].include?(type)` and `!options.key?(:default)`; trails schema-definitions.ts:1031-1037 inlines the type equality checks and tests `options.default === undefined`. The presence check is preserved under the nil↔null mapping: an explicit `default: null` is !== undefined, so it disables the rewrite exactly as Rails' key?-present nil does; the only unmatched shape is an explicit `default: undefined`, which has no Ruby analogue and conventionally means absent in JS.
